name: 53-tally-cli
prompt:
Write tally.py, a command line word counter run as `python3 tally.py [options] FILE`. Six rules, all of which are checked:
1. A word is a maximal run of the characters A-Z a-z 0-9 and underscore; every other byte separates words. Words are counted and printed lowercased.
2. With no options it prints one line per distinct word as `<count> <word>` with a single space between, sorted by count descending and, for equal counts, by word ascending.
3. `--min N` drops words whose count is below N.
4. `--top N` keeps only the first N lines, applied after --min and after sorting.
5. `--exclude a,b,c` drops those words, matched case-insensitively; an empty item in the list is ignored. Options may appear in any order and before or after FILE.
6. If FILE cannot be opened, print exactly `tally: no such file: <FILE>` to stderr and exit 2, writing nothing to stdout. Otherwise exit 0, and an empty file prints nothing at all.
words.txt is in the directory to try it on.

files.words.txt:
The quick brown fox.
the QUICK fox_1 jumps over the lazy dog!
the quick brown fox; the-quick
42 42 42 done

check:
set -u
fail() { echo "FAIL: $1"; exit 1; }
cat > .want0 <<'WANT_EOF'
5 the
4 quick
3 42
2 brown
2 fox
1 dog
1 done
1 fox_1
1 jumps
1 lazy
1 over
WANT_EOF
python3 tally.py words.txt > .got0 2>.err0 || fail 'case 0 exited nonzero'
cmp -s .got0 .want0 || fail 'case 0 output: words.txt'
test ! -s .err0 || fail 'case 0 wrote to stderr'
cat > .want1 <<'WANT_EOF'
5 the
4 quick
3 42
2 brown
2 fox
WANT_EOF
python3 tally.py --min 2 words.txt > .got1 2>.err1 || fail 'case 1 exited nonzero'
cmp -s .got1 .want1 || fail 'case 1 output: --min 2 words.txt'
test ! -s .err1 || fail 'case 1 wrote to stderr'
cat > .want2 <<'WANT_EOF'
5 the
4 quick
3 42
WANT_EOF
python3 tally.py --top 3 words.txt > .got2 2>.err2 || fail 'case 2 exited nonzero'
cmp -s .got2 .want2 || fail 'case 2 output: --top 3 words.txt'
test ! -s .err2 || fail 'case 2 wrote to stderr'
cat > .want3 <<'WANT_EOF'
5 the
4 quick
WANT_EOF
python3 tally.py --min 2 --top 2 words.txt > .got3 2>.err3 || fail 'case 3 exited nonzero'
cmp -s .got3 .want3 || fail 'case 3 output: --min 2 --top 2 words.txt'
test ! -s .err3 || fail 'case 3 wrote to stderr'
cat > .want4 <<'WANT_EOF'
3 42
2 brown
2 fox
1 dog
1 done
1 fox_1
1 jumps
1 lazy
1 over
WANT_EOF
python3 tally.py --exclude The,quick words.txt > .got4 2>.err4 || fail 'case 4 exited nonzero'
cmp -s .got4 .want4 || fail 'case 4 output: --exclude The,quick words.txt'
test ! -s .err4 || fail 'case 4 wrote to stderr'
cat > .want5 <<'WANT_EOF'
4 quick
3 42
WANT_EOF
python3 tally.py --exclude the --min 2 --top 2 words.txt > .got5 2>.err5 || fail 'case 5 exited nonzero'
cmp -s .got5 .want5 || fail 'case 5 output: --exclude the --min 2 --top 2 words.txt'
test ! -s .err5 || fail 'case 5 wrote to stderr'
: > .empty
python3 tally.py .empty > .gote 2>&1 || fail 'empty file exited nonzero'
test ! -s .gote || fail 'empty file printed something'
python3 tally.py missing.txt > .gotm 2>.errm; rc=$?
test "$rc" = 2 || fail "missing file exit $rc, want 2"
test ! -s .gotm || fail 'missing file wrote to stdout'
grep -qx 'tally: no such file: missing.txt' .errm || fail 'missing file stderr'
exit 0
